To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the websites of medical technology companies are a space where the companies can develop relationships with three types of stakeholders, namely investors, healthcare providers, and patients.

websites are a space where medical technology companies enroll three types of online stakeholders into their innovation commercialization strategies, and that these virtual interactions are characterized by the reinforcement of traditional relationships with investors and the creation of proactive roles for healthcare professionals and patients.

the websites of four Canadian medical technology firms are designed to enroll investors, healthcare professionals and patients as stakeholders in the development and uptake of their medical devices, but that the relationships with investors are stereotypical, and that the roles of healthcare providers and patients are more proactive than in traditional healthcare settings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways that websites contribute to building relationships that may be beneficial for companies, but also raise ethical concerns.
how medical technology companies use websites as a tool to build relationships with stakeholders, and how these relationships are perceived as ethically problematic.

the ways in which websites are used to develop relationships with different stakeholders, the nature of the relationships that are created, and the consequences of such relationships for the medical technology sector and society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the websites of medical technology companies are not a neutral space where stakeholders can engage in a meaningful dialogue.
websites are a powerful tool for medical device companies to enroll stakeholders in their innovation development and uptake.
the websites are not neutral communication channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the medical device companies' websites have the potential to create a new space for interaction between the company and its three stakeholders.
websites are a powerful tool to build and reinforce relationships with stakeholders, but the nature of the relationship that is built is not always in the best interest of all parties.
the medical technology companies’ websites are not a neutral space for interaction and relationship building.
The main takeaway from our work is that
websites are a space for companies to engage in a form of social engineering that is not always in the interest of patients and the public.
the websites are not just a communication space, but a place where companies seek to enroll stakeholders into their innovation strategies.
the medical technology companies’ websites may not be as neutral as they claim to be.
